title: Can You Drive Yourself Home After a Root Canal?
metaTitle: Can You Drive Yourself Home After a Root Canal?
metaDescription: Can you drive yourself home after a root canal? With local anaesthetic only, usually yes. With sedation, arrange a ride. Here is the difference explained simply.
secondaryKeywords: can you drive after dental freezing
excerpt: After a root canal with local anaesthetic, most people can drive themselves home. If sedation is involved, you will need a ride. Here is why numbness is not the same as impairment.
heroImageAlt: A person getting into the driver's seat of a car on a bright day after an appointment.
bodyHtml:
Can you drive yourself home after a root canal?

If your root canal is done with local anaesthetic only — which is the case for most people — you can usually drive yourself home afterward. Local anaesthetic numbs the area around the tooth but does not affect your alertness, coordination, or ability to react, so having a numb lip or cheek does not impair your driving. The important exception is sedation: if you and your dentist have arranged any form of sedation for the appointment, you should not drive afterward and will need to arrange a ride. Knowing which applies to you ahead of time makes planning the day simple.

Numbness is not the same as impairment

It is easy to assume that because part of your face feels strange, you should not get behind the wheel. But numbness from local anaesthetic is purely a loss of sensation in the treated area — it does not cloud your thinking, slow your reflexes, or affect your vision. Your hands, feet, eyes, and judgement all work normally. This is quite different from sedation, which is specifically intended to alter how alert and relaxed you feel and therefore does affect your ability to drive safely for a period of time.

When you will need a ride

Plan for someone else to drive you if any of the following apply:

  • You are having sedation. Oral, inhaled, or deeper sedation can affect alertness and reaction time, sometimes for longer than you might expect. Arrange transport and, ideally, someone to be with you afterward, following your clinic's instructions.
  • You feel unwell or shaky. Occasionally people feel light-headed or anxious after a dental visit. If you do not feel steady, it is reasonable to wait, have a drink of water, or ask someone to collect you.
  • Your clinic advises it. Always follow the specific guidance your dental team gives for your situation.

How long before the numbness wears off?

Local anaesthetic typically wears off within a few hours, though it varies from person to person. You do not need to wait for it to fade before driving if only local anaesthetic was used, but you should wait before eating so you do not accidentally bite your numb lip, cheek, or tongue.

Can I go back to work after a root canal?

Many people return to work or their usual activities the same day when only local anaesthetic is used, since the main after-effect is mild tenderness around the tooth. If you had sedation, plan to take it easy for the rest of the day. Listen to how you feel, and do not push yourself if you are sore or tired.

Is it safe to drive with a frozen lip and cheek?

Yes — a numb lip or cheek affects sensation only, not the skills driving requires. If anything about how you feel makes you uncertain, though, there is no harm in waiting a little or arranging a lift for peace of mind.

What if I took something to calm my nerves beforehand?

If you took any medication to ease anxiety before your appointment — even something that was not arranged as formal sedation — tell your dental team, because some of these can affect alertness in the same way sedation does. When in doubt, treat it like sedation and arrange a ride. The same caution applies if you did not sleep well or are feeling run down, since fatigue affects driving regardless of the dental work.

Plan the detail when you book

The easiest way to avoid any uncertainty is to confirm the plan when you schedule your appointment: ask whether only local anaesthetic will be used, or whether any sedation is involved, so you can arrange transport accordingly. You can discuss this and anything else with the team at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham, and you can read more about what a visit involves on the clinic's root canal therapy page. A quick question at the booking stage saves any guesswork on the day and lets you line up a lift ahead of time if you need one.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
